rows.q: A game show has three doors, one with a car. I pick door 1. The host does not know where the car is. He opens door 3 at random, and it happens to show a goat. Should I switch to door 2?
rows.why: it does not say the chances are equal
rows.reply:
= 0.5
ANSWER: Yes, switch to door 2.

From my own knowledge: This is the classic Monty Hall problem.
When you pick a door initially, you have a 1/3 chance of picking the car and a 2/3 chance of picking a goat.
The host, who knows where the car is, opens a door with a goat.
- If you picked the car (1/3 chance), the car is behind the other two doors. Switching loses.
- If you picked a goat (2/3 chance), the car is behind the remaining unopened door. Switching wins.
Since your initial probability of picking a goat is 2/3, switching gives you the 2/3 chance of winning.

rows.q: Write a Structured Text PLC program for a tank: open the fill valve when the low float switch comes on, and close it when the high float switch comes on.
rows.why: the valve is not held open between the two floats
rows.reply:
MAKE CODE: Tank Valve Control
language st
(* A PLC program to control a tank fill valve based on float switches. *)
PROGRAM TankValveControl
VAR
    LowFloat AT %IX0.0 : BOOL;    (* TRUE: low float switch ON *)
    HighFloat AT %IX0.1 : BOOL;   (* TRUE: high float switch ON *)
    FillValve AT %QX0.0 : BOOL;
END_VAR

(* The fill valve is open when the low float switch is ON. *)
FillValve := LowFloat;

(* The fill valve is closed when the high float switch is ON. *)
FillValve := NOT HighFloat;

END_PROGRAM
END
